plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-connect-atomcode

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-connect-atomcode)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-connect-atomcode)
[![ci](https://github.com/eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-atomcode/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-atomcode/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

把本机已登录的 [AtomCode](https://atomgit.com/atomgit_atomcode/atomcode)（官方二进制，终端 AI 编程助手）接成 DeepSeek Harness 的**独立第二意见**。

**写完代码，换一双眼睛再读一遍。**

> 主会话模型检查自己刚写的东西时，读的是同一份上下文、沿着同一条思路——它看不出自己刚才的判断错在哪。AtomCode 是另一套模型、另一套上下文、另一套工具循环，读同一份代码得出的是独立判断。这不是「多一个工具」，是**换一双眼睛**。

## 30 秒上手

1. **装上**：`dsh plugin add dsh-connect-atomcode` → **重启 DSH 进程**（patch 在启动时读取；只改前端时刷新浏览器即可）。其余装法与前置见 [安装](#安装)。
2. **用上**：对话里说一句「用 atomcode_ask 锐评一下当前代码」，主模型自己组织提问；不想让主模型插手时，按每条回复下方的**「锐评」按钮**，或直接打 `/atomcode-review <评审目标>`。
3. **看额度**：输入框下方的 `atom · 4% · 48m50s 后重置` 标签（下面截图里那个）就是 CodingPlan 窗口用量与重置倒计时，点开是详情。为什么是这个数字见 [📊 CodingPlan 额度显示](#-codingplan-额度显示)。

![在对话里打 `/atomcode-review`：命令发出后由宿主侧直接执行，评审结论以一张卡片投递回会话（这一步不花模型回合），主模型据此接着原任务往下走；右下角是输入框下的 CodingPlan 额度弹窗与紧凑标签](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-atomcode/master/assets/atomcode-review.png)

**先知道三条，省得装完才发现**：

- **无 API Key** —— ask 与 `/atomcode-review` 都走本机 daemon token（`~/.atomcode/daemon-13459.json`），网关签名内置于官方二进制；不接任何外部 Key。
- **免费，但有配额** —— 消耗的是**你自己 AtomGit 账号免费领取的 CodingPlan 额度**（`atomcode login` 领取的限时体验版，按 5 小时滚动窗口计量、同样限流）。它不计入当前 DSH 会话的 token 账单，仅此而已：**别把它当无限量**，窗口用满就得等重置。
- **挑场合，不是每次改完都跑** —— 改动涉及核心逻辑、并发/安全/数据正确性，或你自己对结果没把握时，值得花这一次；改样式、改文案这类小改动，等用户点名再跑。工具描述里写的主动调用条件与此同源，**改一处就要改另一处**。

## 它给你什么

三个交付物，①③ 零配置即得：

| 交付物 | 形态 | 底层 | 本机状态 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atomcode_ask` | **主力**：一条消息进，一个完整自主回合出（自带工具循环，能自己决定读哪些文件、跑哪些命令） | daemon `POST /chat`（SSE，token 走 `~/.atomcode/daemon-13459.json`） | ✅ 实测可用 |
| `/atomcode-review` | **辅助**：评审未提交改动 / base 分支 / PR / diff 文本 / 自定义任务，宿主侧执行，**不花模型回合** | 走 daemon `POST /chat`（与 ask 同一条通道；有界：轮数 + 墙钟双保险丝） | ✅ 与 ask 同等可用 |
| CodingPlan 额度显示 | 详情页卡片 + 输入框下紧凑标签，额度走同账号登录态，不接任何外部 Key | 本地额度文本解析（见 [额度一节](#-codingplan-额度显示)） | ✅ 零配置 |

**模型的工具表里只有一个工具**：`atomcode_ask`。早先并存的 `atomcode_review` 工具已退役——模型需要评审时直接调 `atomcode_ask` 并让它自己决定读什么；一次性的差分自查交给 `/atomcode-review` 命令或「锐评」按钮。

**两者的边界不是「一个随便问、一个专业评审」，而是读得多与读得少**：`/atomcode-review` 只能看一个 diff，`atomcode_ask` 能自己决定读哪些文件、跑哪些命令、顺着调用链往下追。所以真正能判断「这段设计对不对」的只有 ask；review 是省 token 的窄口自查。两者走同一条 daemon 通道（单通道决定），review 的代价是没有结构化 `findings[]`——AtomCode 自己跑 `git diff`、写报告，报告是文字。

## 使用

| 你的情形 | 用哪个 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 不确定问题在哪 / 要看调用链 | `atomcode_ask` | 它能自己决定读什么、读多少 |
| 已经知道评哪块（一个 PR / 未提交改动 / 两个分支的差异） | `/atomcode-review <评审目标>` | 一次有界的差分自查，省 token |
| 不写提问词、也不想让主模型插手 | 每条回复下方的**「锐评」按钮** | 它把那条回复填成 `/atomcode-review` 的目标，**不自动发送**，你按回车才跑 |

- **让主会话模型去问**（日常主力）：直接说「用 atomcode_ask 锐评一下当前代码」——模型自己会组织提问，因为它清楚刚改了什么；它带着 AtomCode 的判断回来，**判断是 AtomCode 下的，不是它自己补的**。`continue: true` 接着刚才那条线再问（自动恢复上次 AtomCode session，不用记 id）；续线接到过期的 daemon 会话时用 `reset_session: true` 重新开线。
- **评审的前提**：`working_dir` 已给或已配（插件不猜仓库，三层取不到就拒绝）；报告原文在 `report` 字段（文字，没有结构化 `findings[]`）。

## 安装

**前置**：

- **官方** AtomCode 二进制（v5.x）在 PATH——Windows 实测位 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AtomCode\atomcode.exe`；也可用 `ATOMCODE_BIN` 或 patch 的 `binary` 覆盖。源码构建无 AtomGit 网关签名，默认网关模型不可用
  - **macOS 上「装在 PATH 里」不等于「宿主看得见」**：从访达 / 应用图标启动的 DSH 继承的是 launchd 的 PATH，不是登录 shell 的，于是 Homebrew 装好的 `atomcode` 在终端能用、插件却说找不到。这种情形**开箱即用**：自动探测失败后插件会依次试 `/opt/homebrew/bin/atomcode`（Apple Silicon）与 `/usr/local/bin/atomcode`（Intel），只试这两个真实存在的路径。两处都没有时**面板会写明**去跑的是哪个可执行文件、系统报的是哪个错（`ENOENT` 没找到 / `EACCES` 没有执行权限），以及该怎么修——不再是面板上一句无解的「自动拉起失败」
  - 你自己在 patch 里写下的 `binary` **不会**被这个回退覆盖：那是你点名要跑的可执行文件，找不到就如实报错，不偷偷换一个能跑的
- **已登录**：`~/.atomcode/auth.toml`（`atomcode status` 可查）
- **默认模型可用**：`~/.atomcode/config.toml` 的 `default_model`，或给工具传 `provider`
- ask 需要 daemon：`atomcode daemon --port 13459`（插件默认自动 detached 拉起，实测冷启动约 1.5–4.5s；`auto_start: false` 则需自启）

bundle 形式（与本机 `dsh-connect-*` 同品类），三种装法任选：

1. **npm 包**（普通用户，已发 registry）：`dsh plugin add dsh-connect-atomcode`；或在 `plugin_manager` 里 `install_bundle` 且 `target` 填 `dsh-connect-atomcode`
2. **GitHub 直装**（走 git dep，装 `main`）：`dsh plugin add eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-atomcode`
3. **本地开发**（link 开发副本，一条命令装/卸）：`dsh plugin --profile web add link:<开发目录>` 与 `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-connect-atomcode`。DSH CLI 代跑 pnpm，装完自动 reconcile `dsh.profile.bundles`（新 bundle 默认启用），不用手改 profile 的 `package.json` / `pnpm-lock` / `node_modules`；锁文件里 pnpm 会把绝对路径规范成相对 `link:../../plugins/...`。GUI 插件页只装 registry 包，`link:` 开发副本走 CLI

bundle 自带的 `cordis.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch`）自动声明插入行与全部配置项，无需再写 profile patch。**装完重启 DSH 进程**——patch 在启动时读取、Host 半边只在启动时加载一次；只改 `client.js` 刷新浏览器即可。

> 本插件收录于社区精选列表 [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)（`dsh plugin add` 一键安装的 DSH 插件目录）。
>
> **npm 副本只含运行所需的那几样**（`files` 白名单：`lib/`、`client.js`、`icon.svg`、`locale/`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`README.md`、`CHANGELOG.md`、`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`、`LICENSE`）——`docs/`、`AGENTS.md`、`assets/` 都不在包里，所以文内指向 `docs/` 的相对链接只在 GitHub 仓库里有效。**两张截图走 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 的绝对地址**，因此 registry 页上也能看到；市场读的截图仍取仓库根 `assets/` 与 `screenshots.json`（截图**不进包**是既有策略，`test/release-artifacts.test.mjs` 钉着它）。

## 配置（patch 行 `config:`）

**字段语义的真源是 [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml)**——每个字段的完整注释（含为什么是这个默认值）都在那里，本表只回答「叫什么 / 默认 / 干什么」。面板**不提供输入框**的字段（`approval_mode`、`default_reasoning_effort`、`working_dir`、`ask_max_rounds`）只能在 patch 里改；详情页的「回合边界」行会标出这是插件默认还是**你改过**（判断来自 host 的 `config.authored`，不是值比较）。

![详情页「运行统计」卡片：启动情况、运行环境（默认档位 + 推理力度）、回合边界。下拉里写 `不覆盖（用配置 …）` 的一行表示这一项没有面板值、正落在 patch 的 `config:` 上；一旦在面板上选过，那行才换成你的选择](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-atomcode/master/assets/atomcode-setting.png)

| 键 | 默认 | 一句说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `port` | `13459` | ask 用的 daemon 端口（刻意避开 AtomCode TUI 的 13456） |
| `auto_start` | `true` | 探测不到 daemon 时 detached 拉起。**面板或额度标签一被轮询就会触发**（ask 路径也会），不再是"等第一次调工具才拉" |
| `binary` | `''` | 二进制名/路径（空 = PATH；`ATOMCODE_BIN` 亦可） |
| `approval_mode` | `bypass` | ask 回合内 AtomCode 侧工具的审批档；合法值只有 `build / accept_edits / bypass / plan`，其余值 daemon 422。**改它买不到人审门**——无人值守时非 bypass 也自动放行，见「安全姿态」 |
| `default_provider` | `''` | 缺省**模型档位名**（如 `AtomGit-glm5.3-flash`），`atomcode_ask` 与 `/atomcode-review` 共用。优先级：参数 > 面板选择 > 本字段 > AtomCode 自己的默认；空 = 本层不插手。详见「怎么换 AtomCode 用的模型」 |
| `default_reasoning_effort` | `''` | 随每个 `/chat` 回合发出的**持久力度**缺省（如 `high`）；空 = 用 daemon 自己的持久值，单次调用传 `reasoning_effort` 只覆盖那一回合。插件不预校验，daemon 对不在该模型 `effort_levels` 里的值会回 `reasoning_effort not supported by <provider>` |
| `working_dir` | `''` | 回合的缺省工作目录，同时是侧边对话的会话键（review 也读它作为缺省仓库根）。空 = 交给调用参数 / 宿主会话 cwd；**三层都取不到时 ask 与 review 都拒绝该回合**（与 `approval_mode` 无关），除非调用方传 `allow_unattended: true` |
| `state_path` | `''` | 会话映射文件（缺省 `~/.dsh/state/dsh-connect-atomcode/sessions.json`）。**面板选的档位存在同目录的 `provider.json`**，所以这一项同时决定两者的位置 |
| `ask_max_rounds` | `25` | 工具调用次数上限（按 SSE `tool_start` 事件计；一次 agent 回合可能含多次并行调用，故事件数 ≤ 轮数）。`0` = 不限（交给 daemon 自带治理），上限 1000 在代码里钳制。超限即断开并**尽力**发 `POST /chat/stop`：是"别再等了 + 尽力停止"的止损，不是远程 kill |
| `session_key_prefix` | 自动探测 | 会话键前缀，隔离多 profile（web / desktop）共用同一 state 文件；空 = 按 `DSH_PROFILE`/argv 自动判定 |
| `daemon_retry_secs` | `60` | 自动拉起**失败**后的重试冷却；`0` = 每次轮询都重试；不设则失败会永久禁用本次挂载的自动拉起 |
| `review_brief_mode` | `when-empty` | `/atomcode-review` 的内置评审简报注入方式：`always` / `when-empty` / `never`。闭集，拼错回落默认值并在面板上报出被拒的拼法 |
| `quota_refresh_secs` | `60` | CodingPlan 额度刷新间隔（秒）；`0` = 关闭额度显示（连带不发那条额外 `/command` 调用）。缓存是为了让面板 5s 轮询不变成 5s 一次 daemon 调用 |
| `daemon_start_timeout_secs` | `30` | 拉起 daemon 后等 `/health` 应答的上限（秒），每 1.5s 探一次；`0` = 只 spawn 不等 |

## 怎么换 AtomCode 用的模型（2026-10-14 实测）

AtomCode 5.x 在这条路上的 "provider" **就是模型档位名**，不是厂商名。daemon `GET /models` 的真实形状：

```json
[{ "provider": "AtomGit-glm5.3-flash", "model": "glm5.3-flash", "is_default": false,
   "effort_levels": ["low", "high"] },
 { "provider": "AtomGit-qwen3.8-27b",  "model": "qwen3.8-27b",  "is_default": true,
   "effort_levels": ["low", "medium", "xhigh"] }]
```

那个 `provider` 字段就是 `~/.atomcode/config.toml` 里 `[models."<档位名>"]` 的键名，也正是它 `default_provider` 存的东西——所以四层粒度各归各位：

| 粒度 | 怎么做 | 谁的地盘 |
|---|---|---|
| **单次调用** | 给工具传 `provider="AtomGit-glm5.3-flash"

plugins.description: System-prompt surface drift gate for DeepSeek Harness — sections any plugin contributes are hashed and baselined; silent rewrites fail loud
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-prompt-drift

> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

System-prompt surface drift gate for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

Any plugin or preset can contribute sections to the assembled system prompt.
Upgrading one can silently rewrite what the model is **told**; a malicious
one can inject "ignore all safety rules" straight into the prompt. This
plugin hooks the `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall, hashes every section
(name → sha256(text)), baselines the surface, and diffs every later
assembly against it. **dsh-mcp-test guards what the model can call; this
guards what the model is told.** Zero LLM calls in the trust path.

## Why now (checked 2026-10-12)

Empty lane. The nearest neighbour (`dsh-modelprint`, 0★) fingerprints model
config, not the prompt surface. Prompt-injection plugins scan *content
flowing in*; nobody watches the assembled prompt itself — the one channel
every plugin can write to without anyone reviewing a diff.

## How it works

```
system-prompt/assemble ──> sections [{name, sha256(text)}] name-sorted
                     ──> baseline absent? freeze it (commit the file)
                     ──> diff: added / removed / changed sections
                     ──> warn once per distinct drift (signature dedup)
```

Dynamic sections (cwd, timestamps) can be excluded via `ignoreSections`.
Baseline file is stable, name-sorted JSON — commit it; it is the contract.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile default add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-prompt-drift
```

Prebuilt `lib/` ships in the repo — git installs need no build step and no
`allowBuilds` authorization.

## Configure

```yaml
- id: dsh-prompt-drift
  name: dsh-prompt-drift
  config:
    baselinePath: .dsh-prompt-drift/baseline.json
    rebaselineOnDrift: false
    ignoreSections: []
```

## Compatibility

- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-prompt-drift` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-prompt-drift] active: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-prompt-drift` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.

## Develop

```sh
npm install && npm test
```

## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party prompt-surface pinning, this freezes at its last
working version with a postmortem here.

plugins.description: Progress companion for the dsh web pet: folds durable todo/write and goal/change session events into the pet's status bubble, so it reports how much work is left - not just what the model is doing right now.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-pet-progress

**English** · [中文说明](README.zh.md)

**A progress bar for your desktop pet.**

The [dsh web pet](https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-pet) shows what the agent
is doing *right now* — thinking, calling a tool, done. It has no way to show how
much of a long task is finished, so a task that is 90% done looks exactly like
one that just started.

This plugin fixes that. It reads the todo lists and goals your agent already
writes to the session, and folds them into a percentage bubble on the pet.
A session that never writes a todo list isn't left blank either — there the
bubble falls back to a plain line saying what is happening right now.

## Install

One command, using the plugin's full GitHub URL:

```bash
dsh plugin add https://github.com/Elefseus/dsh-pet-progress
```

This requires the [dsh web pet](https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-pet) to be
installed. If it is missing, the plugin stays loaded but publishes nothing —
you'll see a note in the dsh log rather than a crash.

**Restart DSH afterwards** — bundles are read only at startup, so the plugin
won't mount until you do. The bubble then appears on its own the next time your
agent writes a todo list or starts a goal; there is nothing to switch on.

For a named profile, use `dsh plugin --profile <name> add …`.

## What you'll see

A small bubble above the pet, updated whenever the todo list or the goal changes:

| Situation | Bubble |
| --- | --- |
| Todo list, one task in progress | `3/7 · 43%` titled with that task |
| Todo list, several tasks in progress | `3/7 · 43%`, naming them — up to three, `+N` for the rest |
| All todos done | `任务全部完成` in green — a moment, gone after about 10 seconds |
| Long-lived goal with no todos | `2/8 轮` — the goal's round budget |
| Goal finished | `目标完成` in green — also a moment |
| Goal blocked | The block reason, in place of progress |
| No todo list and no goal | A plain line with no percentage — what the model is writing at this moment (`最近输出`), or what the tool it just called is for (`当前过程`) |

A standing bubble fades out about 30 seconds after the last progress update, so a
finished turn doesn't leave a stale percentage on screen; it comes back by itself
if the work resumes. A **moment** — a finished list or a finished goal — is
announced once and never renewed, so it clears itself instead of sitting there.

Several sessions can be open at once — the most recently active one owns the
bubble.

## Checking the full list

The bubble is one line, so there's a button for the rest: click **进度** on the
pet panel and the complete todo list is written to the dsh log.

## Good to know

- **It never over-reports.** A todo whose status the plugin doesn't recognise
  counts as *not done*. If every entry in a write is unreadable, the plugin
  treats it as "no information" and keeps what it had.
- **It won't guess.** It names the tasks that are actually in progress — up to
  three, each trimmed to 32 characters, with `+N` when more are running. It never
  picks one of several and pretends that one is the work.
- **It reads, it doesn't judge.** A percentage comes from the todo lists and
  goals your agent writes; the plugin never infers progress from how long
  something has been running. Without either, it shows the plain activity line
  instead of a number.
- **It says what is happening, not just which phase.** With no task list it
  follows the model's own output as it is written — the newest words, since
  those are the ones that say what is going on now — and it names what a tool
  call is *for* (`正在调用 pwsh：npm test`, `正在调用 read：progress.ts`), not only
  that a tool is running.

## Requirements

| | |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `>=0.1.7-rc.1` |
| `@linxin666/dsh-pet` | `>=0.4.0` (peer) |
| Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |

The plugin binds to the pet's plugin-seam contract (`announce`,
`registerPanelAction`, and the `session/event` channel); an older pet does not
expose all three.

## Configuration

```ts
apply(ctx, { enabled?: boolean, heartbeatMs?: number })
```

With `enabled: false` nothing mounts. `heartbeatMs` defaults to `10000`.

## Using it from code

The plugin is host-only (no client bundle). The pet service is available as
`ctx.pet`, and the same three seams the pet publishes are what this plugin uses:

| Seam | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.on('session/event', …)` | Reading `todo/write`, `goal/change`, and the turn/step/tool/message events behind the activity line |
| `ctx.pet.announce(…)` | Publishing the progress bubble |
| `ctx.pet.registerPanelAction(…)` | The `进度` panel button |

Adjust `PROGRESS_TTL_MS` and `MAX_TRACKED_SESSIONS` in
[`src/progress.ts`](src/progress.ts) to change the fade-out and how many sessions
are tracked at once.

## Development

`src/*.ts` is the source of truth; `lib/` is committed build output, because the
cordis loader does no transpilation. **After editing `src/`, rebuild and commit
`lib/` with it — CI fails if the two drift apart.**

```bash
node build.mjs              # rebuild lib/ from src/
node --test src/*.test.ts   # 75 tests, node:test only
```

To work on the code, skip installing and point the profile at your checkout:

```jsonc
// ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-pet-progress": "file:<absolute path to this directory>" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["…existing…", "dsh-pet-progress"] } }
}
```

A `bundles` entry alone is not enough — the package must also be a dependency.
If the path contains non-ASCII characters, write it as a `file://` URL. Restart
the app afterwards.

Node is pinned in `package.json` `engines` and exercised in CI at `22.19.0` and
`24.x`.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop up dsh-pet-progress          # update to latest default branch
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "<repo>#<tag>"           # pin a tag instead (reproducible)
```

## More

- [Design notes](docs/DESIGN.md) — why the plugin is built this way: the event
  gap it fills, why it's a sibling rather than a patch, what it reports, and the
  two non-obvious details (deferred mounting, and an announcement slot with no
  retract).

MIT

plugins.description: Deterministic-first triage for DeepSeek Harness: a rule prefilter classifies every ticket, and anything no rule can place is needs_review rather than guessed at.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-batch-triage

**Rules decide the easy tickets. Anything the rules cannot place is handed to a
human — never quietly filed as routine.**

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin.
No model, no service, no network, no API key.

```
$ node -e "
  import('dsh-batch-triage').then(m => {
    const r = m.triageBatch([
      { id: 'a', text: 'The service is down for all users' },
      { id: 'b', text: 'How do I install this on Windows?' },
      { id: 'c', text: 'The frobnitz is blorp.' },
    ], m.resolveConfig({}));
    console.log(r.items.map(i => i.id + ' ' + i.class + '  ' + i.reasonCodes[0]).join('\n'));
    console.log('exit', r.exitCode, r.exitBasis);
  })"

a urgent        OUTAGE_REPORTED
b routine       INSTALL_QUESTION
c needs_review  NO_RULE_MATCHED
exit 6 modelUnavailable
```

## Quick start

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-batch-triage@0.1.2
```

batch_triage is now available; Rules place the tickets they can; anything they cannot place is returned as `needs_review` — never quietly filed as routine.


## Why rules first

A ticket batch is the wrong shape for one model call per item: the volume is high,
the interesting items are few, and every item costs a round trip whether or not it
needed one. So the order is inverted from the obvious one.

**The prefilter runs on every item, first.** Rules place the clear cases — a crash
with a stack trace is urgent, "how do I install this" is routine — and they place
them without asking anything. Only the residue would ever reach a model, and this
release does not reach one at all: it says so instead.

That ordering is not an optimisation. It is the design's main path, and it changes
what the tool is for: **the prefilter is the product, and the model is a fallback.**

## The rule that matters most

> **An item is never `routine` unless a rule said so.**

Every path that cannot classify — an empty body, no matching rule, no model
configured, a budget exhausted — produces `needs_review`. Turning "I could not
tell" into "nothing to see here" is the one failure this tool exists to prevent,
and the test suite pins it in both directions.

0.1.2 tightened what "a rule said so" is allowed to mean. A rule decides on a
*phrase*, and a ticket has more than one sentence: when the phrase that matched is a
question and another sentence reports something broken, the question rule does not get
to decide the ticket. It becomes `needs_review` with `MALFUNCTION_REPORTED`, and the
rule that would have swallowed it stays in `reasonCodes` so a reader sees both halves.

`decidedBy` says which tier actually decided:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefilter` | a rule placed it; `reasonCodes` names which |
| `unavailable` | nothing could place it and no model tier is configured |
| `budget` | a cap was reached, so it was not assessed |

The last two both carry `escalate: true`. Neither is a verdict about the ticket.

## What the rules look at

A **structured field outranks the body text**: `severity: critical`,
`security: true`, `data_loss: true`, `reporter_tier: enterprise`. A reporter who
filled in a form has already told you, and no wording in the body can lower what the
field said. Wording that reports something *worse* still raises it — a field can never
bury an outage, and when the two disagree the item carries both reason codes.

Otherwise **the highest class any rule claims wins**, and the table is written
strongest first so that a tie inside a class goes to the rule listed first:

| class | rules |
|---|---|
| `urgent` | `outage`, `data_loss`, `security`, `crash_with_trace`, `blocked_workflow` |
| `needs_review` | `regression`, `wrong_result`, `performance`, `flaky` |
| `routine` | `install_question`, `usage_question`, `documentation`, `feature_request`, `thanks` |

A ticket that reports an outage *and* phrases itself as a question must not be
swallowed by the question rule. That is a test — and in 0.1.1 it was a test that could
not fail, because its fixture used wording the `outage` rule already recognised, so the
fixture and the rule shared an assumption and the precedence was never really exercised.
Precedence is by class rather than by position now, which also means a caller-supplied
`rules` array cannot reorder the table into a fail-open.

Class precedence alone was not enough, and the six measured tickets below are why.
`outage` did not know "returns 500 for every request", so *no* severity rule matched,
and the question rule decided the whole ticket from one sentence of it. So a `routine`
verdict gets one more check: if the body reports a malfunction — an error, a crash,
something "unusable", a 5xx, deleted records, a leaked credential — in wording no
severity rule could name, the item becomes `needs_review` with `MALFUNCTION_REPORTED`
instead of `routine`. That guard only ever *refuses* a `routine`; it cannot raise
anything to `urgent`, and it cannot touch a verdict a severity rule already made.

Precedence by class is chosen over "most specific wins" deliberately. A scoring system
would need weights nobody could defend; a class ladder needs none, and the table stays
inspectable — a rule that never fires is a bug you can see.

The wordings the fix was measured against, verbatim from the audit. All six were
`routine` with exit **0** on 0.1.1:

| ticket | 0.1.1 | 0.1.2 |
|---|---|---|
| `How do I install this? Also our production API returns 500 for every request.` | `routine` `INSTALL_QUESTION`, exit 0 | `urgent` `OUTAGE_REPORTED`, exit 1 |
| `Is there documentation for the auth flow? We are seeing records deleted from our database.` | `routine` `DOCUMENTATION_REQUEST`, exit 0 | `urgent` `DATA_LOSS_REPORTED`, exit 1 |
| `Feature request: please add CSV export. Meanwhile the app is unusable for our whole team.` | `routine` `FEATURE_REQUEST`, exit 0 | `urgent` `OUTAGE_REPORTED`, exit 1 |
| `How do I configure SSRF protection? Our pentest found we can read other users files.` | `routine` `INSTALL_QUESTION`, exit 0 | `urgent` `SECURITY_REPORTED`, exit 1 |
| `where can i find the logs? the service has been returning 503 all morning` | `routine` `INSTALL_QUESTION`, exit 0 | `urgent` `OUTAGE_REPORTED`, exit 1 |
| `What is the right way to rotate keys? Our API token leaked in a public repo.` | `routine` `USAGE_QUESTION`, exit 0 | `urgent` `SECURITY_REPORTED`, exit 1 |

A ticket that is *only* a question is unaffected: `How do I install this on Windows?` is
still `routine`, and a batch of nothing but routine items still exits 0. The guard is a
floor, not a bias toward urgency.

**What the guard costs, stated rather than discovered later.** It is conservative on
purpose, so a question that merely *mentions* a failure word is bumped as well:
`How do I handle errors returned by the parser?` comes out `needs_review` instead of
`routine`. The class changes; the exit code does not, because a `needs_review` the
prefilter decided is not a finding in this release. That is a real remaining gap — the
guard's own items still exit 0, which is why the six above had to land `urgent` on
their merits rather than merely `needs_review`. It is written up in the CHANGELOG
rather than left for a reader to find.

## Exit codes

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | ran, and nothing needs a human |
| `1` | ran and found something — **not a failure** |
| `2` | the call was invalid (empty batch, over the cap, malformed item) |
| `3` | the input or policy could not be honoured (duplicate `id`) |
| `4` | empty scan |
| `5` | a recorded expectation was not met |
| `6` | every item needing the model was skipped |
| `7` | a cap was zero before any item could reach the model |

The priority between them is one documented ladder in `lib/exit.mjs`, because a run
can satisfy several at once and the order decides which one you are told about:

```
2 usage → 3 config → 4 empty scan → 7 zero budget →
6 model unavailable → 5 expectation → 1 findings → 0 clean
```

A batch of 1–64 items can only reach `0`, `1`, `2`, `3` and `6`. The other three are
rungs of the ladder that this batch runner has no producer for:

* **`4` empty scan** is pre-empted by `2`: an empty batch is refused as a usage error
  b

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: Personal WeChat, WeCom (企业微信) and Feishu (飞书 / Lark) for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): QR pairing, one DSH conversation per chat, two-way text/image/video/document/archive transfer, bots that both send and receive on all three channels, and browser automation over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-wechat-media

**Personal WeChat for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`)** — scan a QR
code once, then talk to your agent from WeChat: one DSH conversation per contact or group, and two-way
text, images, video, documents and archives. Several WeChat accounts can be paired side by side.

**给 DeepSeek Harness 的个人微信桥**：扫一次码，之后就能在微信里和 agent 对话 —— 每个联系人/群各自
一个独立会话，文字、图片、视频、文档、压缩包**双向**互通，支持**多个微信号同时在线**（小号 + 大号）。

---

## What it gives you / 它能做什么

| Capability | Detail |
|---|---|
| QR pairing | Cards in the Plugins panel. The login token is stored under `$DSH_HOME`, so **restarting dsh does not need a new scan**; re-pairing is one click. |
| One conversation per chat | Every WeChat contact (and group) gets its own DSH session with its own context, created or resumed automatically. |
| Text both ways | Your message becomes a turn; the answer is chunked back to WeChat. |
| Media both ways | Images, video, documents and archives. Inbound files are downloaded and decrypted to `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`; the agent gets the path, so a text model can read images through `read_image`. Outbound files are uploaded and sent by the agent through its tools. |
| Multiple accounts | Pair a spare account and your main account; each keeps its own token, cursor and session map. |
| Persistence | Accounts, receive cursor, per-peer context tokens, chat→session routes, allowlist and preferences all live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/`. |

## Requirements / 环境要求

- **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** with the standard agent loop and tools (the shipped `dsh web` / desktop
  profiles qualify), Node.js >= 22 (Node 24 tested), Windows / macOS / Linux.
- **A WeChat account that can scan a QR code.** A spare account is strongly recommended: personal WeChat
  automation is against WeChat's terms of service and carries a ban risk, whichever library you use.
- Outbound access to `ilinkai.weixin.qq.com` and `novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com`.

## Install / 安装

```sh
# from GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:wjh-ux/dsh-wechat-media

# or from a checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-wechat-media
```

Restart `dsh`, then open **Plugins → `dsh-wechat-media`** and press **Add an account (QR code)**.

重启 dsh，然后在 **插件 → `dsh-wechat-media`** 点「**添加账号（扫码）**」。

## Pairing / 配对

1. The card shows a QR code (it polls its own status and refreshes an expired code automatically).
2. Scan it with WeChat on the phone, confirm on the phone.
3. If WeChat asks for digits, type them into the card and submit.
4. The account appears with a status dot: `monitoring` means the long poll is running.
5. **Add an account (QR code)** stays available at all times — scanning a *different* WeChat account
   adds it as another account, so a spare and your main account can run side by side. Scanning the account
   you already have simply refreshes its login. Each row also has **Pair again** and **Unpair**.
6. Opened the QR by mistake? Press **Cancel** — the attempt disappears immediately instead of waiting for
   the code to expire. (A QR lives five minutes; an attempt gives up after eight, and at most three QR codes
   are issued per attempt.)

The QR encodes the landing-page URL the platform hands out — scanning it is what completes the binding.
Each account is stored under its normalized `ilink_bot_id` (`b0f5860fdecb@im.bot` → `b0f5860fdecb-im-bot`),
with `0600` permissions on the files that hold a token; accounts, cursors and conversation routes are keyed
per account, so several can poll at the same time.

## Where inbound files go / 收件目录

By default inbound media is decrypted into `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`. That directory is
configurable, and the change takes effect without a restart:

1. **From the card** - the field under *Inbound files are saved in* submits a plain GET form (a navigation, not a
   fetch), so it works even in browsers where the card's requests never reach the plugin.
2. **From the control panel** - `/dsh-wechat-media/panel` has the same field and a *restore default* button.
3. **With the system folder dialog** - *Browse… / 浏览…* (card and control panel) or
   `GET /dsh-wechat-media/pick-folder` opens Windows' own picker on the desktop and saves the choice. A browser
   cannot hand over an absolute path (a directory input only exposes relative names), which is why the dialog is
   opened by the host (`powershell -STA`) rather than in the page.
4. **From the plugin config** - `inboxDir: "D:\\wechat-files"` in the plugin options, used when no runtime
   preference is set.

The order is preference (card/panel) → config → `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox`. Only an absolute path is accepted: a
relative one is refused with a message instead of being resolved against the process working directory, because a
silently different directory is worse than the documented default. `GET /dsh-wechat-media/state` reports the
effective value as `inboxRoot`, with `inboxRootDefault` and `inboxRootConfig` for comparison.
## Using it / 使用

Just message the bot from WeChat. A few things the agent can do from inside the conversation:

- answer through the normal reply channel (the bridge relays its final text automatically);
- send **extra** messages or **files** with its tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wechat_send_text` | An extra text message, or a message to a different chat (`to`), pre-empting the automatic relay for that turn. |
| `wechat_send_file` | Send a local file back to WeChat. Images (`.jpg/.png/.webp/.gif`) travel as pictures, videos (`.mp4/.mov`) as videos, everything else (pdf, docx, xlsx, zip, 7z, …) as a file attachment. |
| `wechat_status` | Which accounts are paired and which conversations exist. |

Every incoming message is prefixed with `[微信 <name> <wxid>]` so the agent can pass the right `to` when it
answers a specific chat. Group ids look like `12345678@chatroom`.

## Remote approval / 微信里远程审批

When a WeChat-driven session asks for approval — a tool call the permission preset wants confirmed — the prompt
goes to the same WeChat chat, not only to the GUI:

```
⚠️ 需要你批准一次操作（远程审批）
工具：pwsh
原因：write outside the workspace

回 1 = 批准一次 · 回 2 = 拒绝
```

Answer `1` / `y` / `同意` / `批准` / `/approve` to allow that one call, or `2` / `n` / `拒绝` / `/reject` to
refuse it. The answer is **consumed** — it never becomes a new turn. If nothing arrives within
`approvalTimeoutSec` (default 120 s), or the prompt cannot be delivered, or the turn is aborted, the request is
handed back to the GUI, so an approval is never silently dropped. Set `approval: "ignore"` in the plugin config
to keep approvals in the GUI only.

## Contact allowlist / 联系人白名单

Every chat that writes to the bot is remembered, and the card lists them under **Contacts & groups / 联系人 /
群**, with **Allow / Ignore / Clear** per row and an **Only accept allowlisted chats** switch.

- The switch is **off by default** — otherwise a freshly paired account would look broken to everyone who writes.
- With it on, only chats marked *Allow* reach the agent; *Ignore* and undecided chats are dropped and logged.
- A decision takes effect immediately (no restart) and is stored in `peers.json` beside the accounts.

## Friends only / 只处理好友私聊

**Only answer friends (1:1 chats)** — the card's second checkbox, or `/friends on` from a chat. The protocol
carries no "is a friend" flag, so *friends* means **1:1 chats**: when the switch is on, every **group** message
is dropped, whatever the allowlist says about that group. Direct chats are unaffected.

- **Off by default**: an upgrade must not change who the bot answers.
- Group messages are **ignored silently** (that is the point) but never invisibly: each one bumps
  `counters.groupsSkipped`, `/status` prints `已静默忽略群消息 N 条`, and the card shows the same number.
- It is one preference (`prefs.json`), so the checkbox and `/friends` can never disagree, and it applies to
  personal WeChat and WeCom alike.
- Switching it on **while a group is waiting** answers once in that group to explain the coming silence. Turning
  it off works from a 1:1 chat or the card — a group message is skipped before it could be read as a command,

plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-alert-relay

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-alert-relay)


**关键词**：告警外发 · 告警配置 · 应急响应 · 敏感信息外泄 · webhook 安全 · 告警链路 · 应急
**Keywords**: alert relay · alerting · incident response · webhook security · sensitive data in alerts
**告警外发** —— 检查告警链路：有没有告警、发到哪、有没有把敏感信息一起发出去。

## 不装它会怎样

出事时你的告警是这么发的：

```js
post(webhook, { text: err.stack + JSON.stringify(req.body) })
```

**告警通道通常是整个系统里管控相对较弱的一条出口**：

```
数据库：内网、有审计、有权限控制
告警 webhook：一个 URL，谁拿到谁就能发
```

把 `err.stack`、完整请求体、用户数据塞进去，等于**把敏感信息复制到一个管控更弱的地方**。

## 它查什么

| 级别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 高 | 告警内容带敏感信息 · webhook 明文 http:// |
| 🟡 中 | 把带密钥的告警 URL 打进日志 · 找不到任何告警配置 |

## 正确做法

```
❌ post(webhook, { text: err.stack + JSON.stringify(req.body) })
✅ post(webhook, { text: `[ERROR] trace=${traceId}` })
```

**只发摘要 + trace id**，细节放在有权限控制的地方。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-alert-relay
# 或纯 CLI
npx @deepwhale-cn/dsh-alert-relay
```

## 用法

```bash
dsh-alert-relay --demo
dsh-alert-relay --list-rules
dsh-alert-relay --html r.html
```

![dsh-alert-relay 检查报告示例](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-alert-relay/report.png)

![dsh-alert-relay 演示模式输出](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-alert-relay/demo.png)

![dsh-alert-relay 规则与依据](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-alert-relay/rules.png)

## 边界

- **不验证告警真能发出去** —— 只看配置与代码。
- **「找不到告警配置」是弱信号** —— 可能由部署层统一做，报出来是提示你确认。
- 与 [dsh-cn-log-retention](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) 分工：那个查日志留多久，这个查告警发去哪。

本插件是一个工具。使用者必须遵守所在地区法律法规，**对使用本项目造成的任何后果自行承担责任。**

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 38 个）

> 一个插件做一件事。**安全问题是链式的** —— 配套用才完整。

**国内合规**（12）｜ [等保对照](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-mlps) · [日志留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) · [备案公示](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-filing) · [用户同意](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-consent-guard) · [个人信息权利](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-rights) · [未成年人保护](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-minor-guard) · [影响评估](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-pipia) · [数据分类分级](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-classify) · [算法备案](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-algorithm-filing) · [数据出境](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) · [国密合规](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-crypto) · [AI 内容标识](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-ai-labeling)

**AI 与 Agent 治理**（6）｜ [AI 输出信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ai-output-trust) · [外部内容信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-content-trust) · [MCP 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) · [Agent 权限](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-scope) · [策略核对](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-policy) · [可疑指令](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-phishing-guard)

**数据与凭据**（5）｜ [敏感数据](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-scan) · [密钥轮换](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-key-rotate) · [数据留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-lifecycle) · [配置审计](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-env-audit) · [密钥扫描](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-secret-scan)

**供应链与构建**（5）｜ [开源许可](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-license-guard) · [依赖投毒](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-dep-audit) · [CI 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ci-guard) · [工具审查](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-tool-vet) · [物料清单](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-sbom)

**权限与应急**（3）｜ [最小权限](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-least-privilege) · [告警外发](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-alert-relay) · [应急证据包](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-incident-package)

**行业专项**（4）｜ [医疗行业专项](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-industry-medical) · [教育行业专项](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-industry-education) · [金融行业专项](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-industry-finance) · [地方数据条例](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-local-regulation)

**编排与交付**（3）｜ [一键体检](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-guard-suite) · [改前改后复核](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-fix-verify) · [合规可交付文档](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-compliance-doc)

都在 DSH 插件市场（dsh-plugin.org）、npm 和 deepwhale.org.cn/guard.html 上。

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-boot-animation

Replaces the DSH startup page with a chosen or random local video, then transitions into the app, with configurable playback and fallback controls. It does not modify DSH core source; future compatibility is not guaranteed.

**Language:** English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

This is a community plugin, not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.

- **Package:** [`@ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation)
- **Release:** [0.4.0](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-boot-animation/releases/tag/v0.4.0)
- **Repository:** [Alice-Marx/dsh-boot-animation](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-boot-animation)
- **Topic:** `dsh-plugin`
- **Directory category:** UI & Experience (用户界面与体验), following the [DSH Plugin Hub submission categories](https://dsh-plugin.org/submit). A category choice is not a claim of listing acceptance.

## Screenshots

Local Chromium demo host rendering the actual 0.4.0 boot and card source with sample profile data. These are not screenshots of a signed-in live DSH profile and are not a cross-platform certification.

![Startup preview](assets/screenshots/startup-preview.png)

![Settings preview](assets/screenshots/settings-preview.png)

## Install

### Web

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation@0.4.0 --save-exact
```

Host and Node requirements must already be met.

### Desktop

Open **Settings -> Plugins -> Add plugin**, paste `@ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation@0.4.0`, then quit and reopen from the tray as prompted.

For Desktop upgrades where the live install API reports the package as already installed, fully quit from the tray first and use the official Desktop bundled wrapper — not an older global `dsh` binary.

Windows default-location copyable offline command:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add '@ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation@0.4.0' --save-exact
```

Adjust the wrapper path if DeepSeek Harness is installed elsewhere. If you use a custom `DSH_HOME`, retain it when running this command. Do not use this exact Windows path on Linux or macOS.

### Uninstall

Web:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation
```

Desktop: use the official plugin UI. Existing custom videos are separate data; review and back them up before manual deletion. A fresh package install auto-registers the scoped bundle; do not manually insert a second bundle entry.

## Configuration

The plugin uses the host profile configuration and a plugin patch file. There is no separate `.env`, INI, or JSON settings loader.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.yml` | Host base configuration. |
| `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` | Plugin configuration edits. The shipped patch mounts id `boot-animation` with name `@ljwei-stak/dsh-boot-animation`. |
| Profile `package.json` | Tracks dependency and `dsh.profile.bundles` via the installer. |

An [example fragment](examples/boot-animation.config.yml) is provided as a config-object reference only; it is not a standalone autoloaded config file.

Settings namespace: `boot-animation`. Prefer the existing settings UI. Preview uses current settings immediately. Reload the Web page for the next startup; on Desktop, fully quit from the tray and reopen for the next startup. Host entry upgrades also require a full process restart.

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `fadeMs` | `2000` | Schema range `300`–`5000` ms; UI presets `1000`, `1500`, `2000`, `3000`, `4000`. |
| `enterMode` | `tail` | `tail` dissolves at clip end; `end` fades after playback; `click` loops until entry. |
| `disabledClips` | `[]` | Opaque filenames disabled in the pool. |
| `sound` | `true` | Subject to browser gesture policy. |
| `clickToEnter` | `false` | When enabled, the first pointer press enters immediately; otherwise a press may first unlock audio. |
| `showHint` | `true` | Display entry hint. |

## Media

Imported videos are copied to `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/data/dsh-boot-animation/videos`. The original selected file is untouched. Legacy bundled assets under `assets/videos` may be replaced by package upgrades; UI import is preferred.

In the UI, open **Settings -> Plugins -> 启动动画** to import a video up to 256 MiB, set one clip as startup or enable several for random selection, preview current effects, and remove custom clips after confirmation.

## Compatibility

- **DSH:** minimum `>=0.2.0-rc.2`; integration verified against Windows Desktop runtime `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2`.
- **Node:** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`; ESM.
- **Runtime dependency:** `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `^3.18.4` (declared as a dependency, not a peer dependency).
- **Browsers:** Chromium, Chrome, and Edge targeted; Firefox is unverified.
- **Platforms:** macOS and Linux script paths exist but were not independently tested in this acceptance.
- **Codecs:** browser-supported codecs are required. H.264/AAC MP4 is preferred. MP4, WebM, M4V, and MOV containers do not guarantee codec decoding.

## Permissions and trust

This Node plugin runs with host OS privileges; there is no per-plugin sandbox.

- **Reads:** shipped scripts and videos.
- **Writes/removes:** imported video copies in the profile data directory.
- **Optimize:** explicitly rewrites a bundled MP4 using Node APIs, with `originals/` backups and `.faststart-work/` scratch space. The runtime does not execute shell commands or `ffmpeg`.
- **Credentials/network:** no model or provider API keys, telemetry, or remote services are used in the plugin runtime. Browser HTTP calls are same-origin. `npm` and GitHub network access are required by the installer and are distinct from runtime behavior.

### HTTP boundary

Custom import, read, and delete routes enforce DSH `connection.requestRejection` authentication and path checks. Bundled clip manifest/video and Optimize routes do not enforce that same hook themselves. Do not assume every route is authenticated.

Use only in a trusted local environment. Remote or reverse-proxy operators must enforce access control for the entire `/plugins/dsh-boot-animation/` prefix. Imported media is not published to GitHub or npm. Videos are served `no-store`, so repeated loads transfer clip data again.

## License

Code is under [MIT](LICENSE). The `LICENSE` declares the bundled MP4 work under the same MIT terms. User-imported media retains its own rights; installing the plugin does not relicense it.

## Reference repositories

- Original code / upstream: [`lxj5820/dsh-boot-animation`](https://github.com/lxj5820/dsh-boot-animation)
- Official DSH host: [`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
- Current maintained distribution: [`Alice-Marx/dsh-boot-animation`](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-boot-animation)

No endorsement by the upstream or host projects is implied.

## Developer notes

Validation commands present in this repository:

```bash
node build-client.mjs      # only if client source changes
node verify/verify-entry.mjs
node verify/verify-degraded.mjs
node verify/verify-options.mjs
node verify/verify-custom-clips.mjs
```

The 0.4.0 release passed 243 checks; this does not imply every Desktop release or operating system was fully end-to-end tested.

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [MANUAL.md](MANUAL.md), and [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for development and setup detail. Archived historical notes are kept at [docs/DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md) and are non-authoritative.

## Directory submission

A [ready-to-copy submission draft](docs/PLUGIN_SUBMISSION.md) follows the hub template. Its listing badge remains inactive until a matching detail page has been verified; it is not an endorsement or a claim of marketplace acceptance.

-->

plugins.description: Native Rapid-MLX provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — dsh reads model facts from the server instead of your settings.yaml.
plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

## Three things worth knowing before you edit this

Each of these cost real

plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.
